section_summary: This final section completes an English translation of Japan’s Ministry of International Trade and Industry Establishment Law, covering resource and mine-safety offices, the industrial science and technology and patent agencies, government corporations, personnel, repealed regulations, transitional provisions, and ministerial signatures. It also contains an August 1949 State Department memorandum recommending reconsideration or reform of American administration of the Ryukyu Islands. The section ends with a September 1949 despatch from the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan concerning implementing ordinances for the new ministry.

subfiles.title: Ministry of International Trade and Industry Establishment Law (continuation)
subfiles.about: Continuation and conclusion of the statute establishing the organization, functions, auxiliary bodies, personnel system, and subordinate corporations of Japan’s Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
subfiles.summary: The text continues with local coal, mine-safety, and coal-mine inspection offices under the Resources Agency, followed by the Agency of Industrial Science and Technology and its councils. It defines the organization and responsibilities of the Patent Agency, its examination and judgment divisions, Exhibition House, and patent-related committees, then addresses the Smaller Enterprise Agency, ministry personnel, and government corporations known as Kodan. Supplementary provisions make the law effective on May 25, 1949, repeal numerous earlier laws and ordinances, establish transitional arrangements, and conclude with the signatures of Finance Minister Ikeda, Agriculture and Forestry Minister Mori, Commerce and Industry Minister Inagaki, and Prime Minister Yoshida.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Ryukyus
subfiles.from: Unidentified U.S. Department of State official; drafted in Far Eastern Affairs by D. L. Oliver
subfiles.about: Recommends reconsideration of U.S. retention of the Ryukyus and immediate reform of the islands’ American military government.
subfiles.summary: Memo: ambiguous policy and weak military government are increasing Ryukyuan demands for return to Japan. It recommends reviewing retention, otherwise integration with Japan, senior leadership and reforms.

subfiles.title: Despatch concerning implementation of the Ministry of International Trade and Industry Establishment Law
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits or discusses Japanese ordinances implementing the recently enacted Ministry of International Trade and Industry Establishment Law.
subfiles.summary: Degraded despatch on implementing the Ministry of International Trade and Industry Establishment Law of May 24, 1949; enclosed documents did little to clarify organization.
